assertion_audit.assertions: Both generations, noninterleaving rows, timestamps present/finite/ordered, valid snapshot index, single stop and request.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Absent replacement, overlapping generations, missing/nonfinite/reordered timestamps, invalid earlier_count, or missing/duplicated lifecycle anchors violate the respective assertion; removing timestamp/request checks prevents the refusal controls at 575-588 from raising.

assertion_audit.assertions: First post-request row is replacement; row does not precede request; at most two rounded elapsed instants and two consecutive missing instants.
assertion_audit.fails_if: An incumbent row at 8.5 after request 8.25 fails identity; replacement at 11.1 after 8.25 fails rounded elapsed; missing instants 7,8,9 fail consecutive misses; restoring stop-relative timing makes the 6.01-to-10 refusal test fail, but fractional overruns remain accepted.
Changing row counts, request/first-row anchors, floor arithmetic, missed list [8,9], longest gap 2 or selected PID differs from independently fixed literals.

assertion_audit.assertions: Specific refusal for late replacement, excessive misses, incumbent after request and late request-to-delivery despite late stop.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Removing the respective bound, using stop as request anchor, or raising for the wrong reason prevents the expected AssertionError/message.

assertion_audit.assertions: Accept 8.25 and 8.99 against request 6.25; refuse 9.0; literal rounded counts; first_row_slot equals input row_slot.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Changing rounded arithmetic or selecting lifecycle sample=90 instead of the row fails the literal counts; exact fractional validation rejects 8.99, revealing the blocking contract mismatch; the final equality is an input echo, not an independent timing guard.

assertion_audit.assertions: Require request and row timestamp anchors.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Removing either validation prevents its corresponding absent-anchor fixture from raising the specified refusal.

assertion_audit.assertions: First row instant=7, elapsed=1, PID=22, missing run=0 despite later replacement rows.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Selecting the last replacement row or measuring observer time instead of the first row changes literal counters when four later rows exist.

assertion_audit.assertions: Missing instants [7,9] and longest run 1 across later incumbent row.
assertion_audit.fails_if: Starting gap accounting only at the last incumbent drops instant 7; treating separated gaps as consecutive reports 2 instead of 1.

findings.text: blocking: Flooring both request_slot and first_slot before enforcing <=2 permits almost three elapsed sampling periods, violating the live plan's within-two-periods rehearsal. The new passing boundary case at lines 558-572 uses request=6.25 and row=8.99: elapsed is 2.74 periods (27.4 seconds at the ten-second cadence), but floor(8.99)-floor(6.25)=2. Restore the fractional elapsed bound independently of the whole-instant missing-sample counter, and require this overrun to be refused.

non-blocking: counts['first_row_slot'] == row_slot compares returned metadata directly with the same row_slot inserted into rows at line 561; it still passes if the elapsed-time guard is removed or rounded, so this equality must not be counted as an independent regression guard. The adjacent literal instant assertions exercise the chosen counter arithmetic; independent fractional refusal belongs to the blocking finding.
